product.name: netMind Extension
product.description: AI browser agent — chat with pages, automate tasks, multi-provider LLM support.

mcp._why: Names the MCP server in mcp-server/ derives at build time (scripts/brand.mjs). serverName and packageName override the slug-based defaults (netmind-extension); the rest equals what product.shortName would derive. Tools become <toolPrefix>_run/_extract/_status/_respond/_abort/_connection, hosts show them as mcp__<skillName>__<toolPrefix>_*.

services._whyBackendBaseUrl: netMind Extension backend (deploy/netmind_extension_backend): verifies the Viettel SSO ID token and issues the LiteLLM model key. Replaces the former Second Brain service.
services._whyLitellmBaseUrl: Fallback only. The backend returns an authoritative baseUrl on every provision and that value wins, so this matters just for a client that has a key but has not provisioned yet. Already ends in /v1, so nothing is appended.
services._whyOidcEndpoints: The Viettel SSO wrapper publishes no /.well-known/openid-configuration, so the two endpoints discovery would have supplied are named here. Set both or neither.
services._whyOidcIdTokenAlg: The wrapper signs ID tokens with HS256 and serves no JWKS, so the extension cannot check the signature. Pinning the header alg at least refuses a token swapped to `none` or to an alg this deployment never issues.
services._whyOidcBearerToken: Which token the backend can verify. With the provider fully named in this config, sign-in never consults the backend's /api/auth/providers — this value alone decides what gets sent, so it must match how the backend verifies (the advertised bearer_token only reaches installs whose config names no provider). The wrapper signs ID tokens with a secret it gives nobody, so the backend verifies by calling the wrapper's /userinfo instead — and /userinfo recognises only the opaque access token it minted, answering 401 'Token not found or expired' for an ID token that was never in any store to be found. Set back to id_token the day the wrapper publishes a JWKS and the backend checks signatures locally again.
services._whyOidcSendNonce: The Viettel SSO wrapper does not echo the `nonce` back in the ID token, so sending one guarantees a failed sign-in: OIDC Core §3.1.3.7 requires the client to reject a token whose nonce does not match what it sent. `nonce` is OPTIONAL for the authorization code flow, so not sending it is spec-clean — unlike sending one and skipping the check. This DOES give up a layer of replay protection; PKCE S256, the verified `state`, and an ID token that arrives over the back channel rather than the browser redirect carry the rest. Set this back to true the day the wrapper echoes the nonce.

replacements._why: Temporarily shield upstream API header names from display-name replacement.

Upstream sells a hosted tier next to the extension, so its provider is labelled "WebBrain Cloud". netMind has no such split — the managed gateway is simply what the product runs on — and letting the rule below rename only the first word leaves "netMind Extension Cloud" in the model picker. Must stay ahead of that rule, which would otherwise consume the WebBrain half first. Only the two-word display name is matched: the provider id webbrain_cloud, api.webbrain.one and the X-WebBrain-* headers carry no space and are untouched.

The agent indicator's header comment describes its cursor as "WebBrain-purple". The colour rules further down recolour it to raspberry, so the wording has to go too — and it has to go here, ahead of the display-name rule, which would otherwise leave the dangling "netMind Extension-purple".
Display name in UI and skill text. Guards keep it out of identifiers and protocol tokens such as ensureWebBrainGroup and X-WebBrain-Help-Improve.
Restore upstream API header names after display-name replacement.
Lowercase brand name inside translated sentences. Scoped to locale files only; the lookarounds keep it off webbrain.one, webbrain_note and webbrain-tools.

The agent's on-page indicator — the pulsing viewport border, the stop button and the target cursor — is upstream's indigo #6c63ff. It is a content script injected into the page with no imports, so it cannot read the theme's CSS variables and the colours have to be substituted literally. Rules, not a patch: this file is pure colour swapping, so replacement survives upstream rearranging it and catches any accent they add later. rgb() triples first, then the hex spellings.
Same indicator, hex spelling of the accent: the target cursor's SVG fill.
Same indicator: the stop button's hover tint, an indigo wash on white. Brand blush is its raspberry counterpart.
Same indicator: the stop button's label ink, a navy that reads cold beside raspberry. Brand ink instead.
Same indicator: the cursor's shadow and outline strokes, tinted with the same navy. Brand ink keeps them warm.
Keep the indicator's header comment honest about what it now draws — the rules above leave it describing a purple it no longer uses.

The highlight tool's default outline drawn on the page, indigo again. tools.js states the same value in the tool schema the model reads, so both files have to move together or the model would be told a default that no longer exists. Deliberately not applied to sidepanel.js, whose only #7c3aed is console.log styling — red there would read as an error.
The Teach capture badge pinned to the page while a session records: indigo border on a near-black violet chip. Brand raspberry on the dark theme's ink, with paper for the label.
Same badge, its violet-black chip background.
Same badge, its lilac-tinted label text.

The selected-text ask bubble is the third indigo content script, again with every colour written literally inside its closed shadow DOM. Rules, not a patch, for the same reason as the visual indicator: colour swaps survive upstream rearranging the stylesheet and catch any accent they add later. Patch 090 carries only the structural netMind delta (the N-mark logo and popup brand row). This rule is the light accent.
Same bubble, the pressed/hover accent, mapped to the brand accent-hover.
Same bubble, the accent as an rgb() triple (this file writes rgba() without spaces): the selection highlight wash, the button border, and the focus rings.
Same bubble, the accent-strong triple: the highlight's inset hairline.
Same bubble, the lavender row-hover wash. Brand blush, as on the indicator's stop button.
Same bubble, light-theme navy ink and violet-grey neutrals, mapped to the raspberry paper palette: text to brand ink, muted to text-secondary, border to ink at 12% over white.
Same bubble, the two navy shadow triples behind the button and the popup. Brand ink keeps them warm.

Same bubble, dark theme. Upstream's dark block only re-tints neutrals and keeps one indigo accent for both themes; netMind's dark accent is the lightened raspberry, so the swap that moves the surface onto the dark palette also introduces the two accent overrides upstream never declares.
Same bubble, the remaining dark-theme neutrals: text, muted, border.
Fallback prefix for downloaded screenshot filenames.
User-visible export and capture filenames.
Fallback names for recordings and staged screenshots.
Branded workflow exports while continuing to import legacy WebBrain and AgentX WebMate workflow files.
Accept new, previous-brand, and legacy workflow file extensions.

OpenRouter shows the HTTP-Referer next to X-Title on its app leaderboard and in the account dashboard, so this string is read by people outside the extension. X-Title already says netMind Extension; the referer has to agree.

Thai marks sentence breaks with a space and never a terminator, so the rule above has nothing to anchor on in th.js. This is the only locale whose CTA has to be named outright; if upstream rewords the Thai copy, the leftover-webbrain count catches it.

The Ollama origin warning links to upstream's blog post. netMind cannot host that page and must not send users to webbrain.one, so the anchor goes; the warning body and the OLLAMA_ORIGINS snippet above it already carry the actual fix. Leaves st.providers.ollama_warning.link unused, which is harmless.
Send reviews and feedback to the product repository until store listings are available.
Do not show a misleading store-review prompt before netMind Extension has official listings.
Send feedback to the product issue tracker.
Point the in-app documentation link to this repository's documentation.

Strip the whole trailing call-to-action from localized social-share copy. Upstream closes every translation with a localized "Try it:" plus https://webbrain.one, and this text is published to X and LinkedIn, so outsiders read it. netMind posts carry no link, and dropping only the URL would publish a dangling "Try it:" in 23 languages. Anchored to the last sentence terminator before the URL so each locale loses exactly its own phrase.

Vietnamese is the default UI language. Upstream picks the browser language and falls back to English; netMind ships to Vietnamese users whose browsers are mostly en-US, so a saved choice wins and everyone else starts in Vietnamese.
Default locale in exported/imported config, so a config round-trip does not reset the UI to English.
Locale the background worker assumes for the selection shortcut before the user picks one.
Locale the background worker assumes for the selection shortcut before the user picks one (Firefox build).
Selection-shortcut strings fall back to Vietnamese instead of English for unknown locales.
The in-page selection bubble renders before the background answers with the stored locale; start it in Vietnamese instead of the browser language.

Settings > Skills opens on a paragraph that spells out the WebMCP fence names `webbrain-tools` and `webbrain-skill` inside <code> tags, so the upstream brand reaches the screen however the display-name rules are scoped. Those two are protocol identifiers external sites rely on — they stay put in src/agent/skills.js and in the packaged skills, and only the visible copy can move. Rewriting the whole sentence also sheds the catalog/planner/semantic-intent wording it opened with, which is loader detail nobody reading that tab for the first time needs. One rule per locale, since each carries its own translation; the pattern matches the key and whatever value trails it, so an upstream rewording is swallowed rather than quietly restoring the old text.
